sources.citation: Philippson, Gérard. 1991. Tons et accent dans les langues bantu d'Afrique Orientale: étude comparative typologique et diachronique. Thèse d'Etat, Paris V.
sources.note: No Rwa-specific statement: Tableau 1 (p. 73-4) lists 'chaga-ouest (E61, 62a) + : mashami, rwa, siha'; the Annexe prosodic profiles cover only Vunjo and Gweno for the Chaga group (item 10 'accent démarcatif (culmination de longueur)').

sources.citation: Nnko, Elirehema Daniel. 2024. The Tonology of Simple and Complex Infinitives in Meru Language of the Northeastern Tanzania. International Journal of English Literature and Social Sciences 9(1): 34-45. doi:10.22161/ijels.91.5
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. IV p. 36: 'Meru is tone accent language'; lexical and grammatical tone; autosegmental analysis with a tonal 'accent' (H-docking diacritic) assigned to the stem-initial syllable, Basic Tone Melody LHL; 'stress' never mentioned.
sources.venue: International Journal of English Literature and Social Sciences

sources.citation: Nnko, Elirehema Daniel. 2023. Swahili Loanwords in Meru Language of the Northeastern Tanzania: A Phonological Analysis of Nouns. IJELS 8(6): 282-292. doi:10.22161/ijels.86.44
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Gives vowel/consonant inventory, long vowels (p. 287), syllable structure; Swahili penult-stressed vowels are borrowed as long vowels (ada > aada, soda > sooda, p. 290-1).

sources.citation: Shinagawa, Daisuke. 2015. Vowel length and TMA micro-variation in Kilimanjaro Bantu. Asian and African Languages and Linguistics 9: 5-21. TUFS/ILCAA. hdl:10108/80343
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 3.1 p. 11-12: 'Rwa has a clear contrast of vowel length in the anti-penult (7a), penult (7b), and most notably word/sentence-final positions (7c)' -- i.e. no neutralising penultimate lengthening is reported.
sources.venue: Asian and African Languages and Linguistics

sources.citation: Shinagawa, Daisuke [品川大輔]. 2010. キリマンジャロ・バンツー諸語におけるTA標示形式とその変化についての覚書 [Notes on TA markers in Kilimanjaro Bantu]. 香川大学経済論叢 83(1-2): 21-56.
sources.note: Nothing; TA morphology only (アクセント/強勢/声調 = 0 hits).

sources.citation: Shinagawa, Daisuke. 2009. A rare story of the emergence of the Future? A hypothesis on the historical development of Proto-Bantu *-ag in Rwa (Bantu, E61). HERSETEC 2(1): 137-150. Nagoya University.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Fn. 4 (p. 138-9) phoneme inventory and surface-tone notation (H, downstepped H, mid, long falling, long rising, L); sec. 2.1 (p. 141-2) lexical H of Rwa realized one TBU to the right (rightward tone shift).

sources.citation: Philippson, Gérard & Marie-Laure Montlahuc. 2003. Kilimanjaro Bantu (E60 and E74). In Nurse & Philippson (eds), The Bantu Languages, 475-500. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Nothing on stress for any KB language; sec. 2.1 vowel length (Rw. exx. 7-8), sec. 3 tone: tone shift + three-way SH/H/L surface contrast, 'S., Rw. and K. probably do so'; Rwa otherwise barely covered ('Practically nothing has ever been published on.. Rw.').

sources.citation: Shinagawa, Daisuke. 2025. Rwa (E621A), Uru (E622D), and Mkuu (E623C): Less-described varieties of Kilimanjaro Bantu (Chaga) languages. In The Oxford Guide to the Bantu Languages, 851-866. Oxford: OUP.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Most recent and authoritative description of Rwa by the language's main fieldworker; has a phonology section with tone; the Oxford Guide template usually states whether there is stress/penultimate lengthening.
sources.venue: The Oxford Guide to the Bantu Languages
